title.narrative: COVID-19: Ebeye Solid Waste Management Project

description.narrative: The project will establish a sustainable and effective solid waste management (SWM) system in Ebeye, the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), by (i) building a high-temperature incinerator and upgrading the dump site, (ii) upgrading and replacing equipment for municipal solid waste management, (iii) strengthening institutional capacity to sustain the SWM services, The project will also prevent the spreading of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) and other transmittable and waterborne diseases through improved medical waste disposal and strengthened medical waste management capacity. A project readiness financing grant was approved in 2019 to prepare the project and facilitate a smooth transition to the project implementation.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Coverage, and sustainability of integrated SWM service delivery improved in Ebeye

At least 2,200 tons/year of waste, including menstrual and medical waste, incinerated Progress/Status: During the project's MTR in December 2024 and subsequent communications in March 2025, it has been decided that the incinerator package will be removed from the project. A change in scope will be processed for this change. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:
Total annual greenhouse gas emissions from the dump site reduced by 2,688 tCO2 equivalent/year Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

At least 8,400 people (85% of the population) in Ebeyeb covered by the sustainable waste management services, including at least 4,200 women (85% of the female population) Progress/Status: Small works (package W3) for the improvement of the current landfill operations have been completed. Procurement activities for package W2 have been initiated; final draft BD has been prepared and is under review/clearance. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

KALGOV recovers at least 25% of its operational cost from user charges Progress/Status: To enhance the sustainability of KALGOV's SWM operations, the first version of the KALGOV Financial Management Plan was drafted under the project. The proposed tariff framework and fee collection plan have been prepared and is undergoing the required government approvals. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline value: N/A
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: A high-temperature incinerator constructed, and waste disposal site and recycling facility upgraded. Indicator: After the installation of the incinerator, at least three women hired and trained for 12 targeted new positions in the incinerator or landfill operations, e.g., waste sorter, thermal plant operator, and workers Progress/Status: Noted that the incinerator will be proposed to be removed. A minor change is currently under process. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to sustain SWM service delivery and local engagement strengthened Indicator: At least 80% of all high school female students in Ebeye receive training in menstrual health and hygiene (including proper menstrual waste disposal and use of reusable pads) and report increased knowledge and awareness on the subject Progress/Status: Community engagement specialist, community engagement officer has been recruited. Activities ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to sustain SWM service delivery and local engagement strengthened Indicator: At least 80% of the Ebeye population, 50% of whom are women, participate in knowledge events and report increased awareness of anti-littering regulations, 3R, handling of batteries, and waste segregation Progress/Status: Community engagement specialist, community engagement officer has been recruited. Activities ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity to sustain SWM service delivery and local engagement strengthened Indicator: COVID-19-related medical waste management procedures improved and at least 80% of Ebeye Hospital staff members (and 80% of women personnel) receive training and report improved knowledge of and skills in proper handling and disposal of hazardous waste, and in maintaining the safety of patients, personnel, and community Progress/Status: in preparation Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Municipal solid waste collection, transport, and disposal operations improved Indicator: One 8 m3 new waste compactor truck purchased and one compact track loader for the operation of the incinerator purchased and operated with spare parts under a 5-year maintenance and repair service agreement Progress/Status: Truck has been procured. Procurement for the compact truck loader ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: Municipal solid waste collection, transport, and disposal operations improved Indicator: At least 1,020 households in Ebeye (85% of the total households) equipped with wheelie bins with lids and whose waste is collected at least twice a week, including 200 households headed by women (90% of the households headed by women) Progress/Status: Procurement of bins has been completed and distributed. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Actual value:

Output: A high-temperature incinerator constructed, and waste disposal site and recycling facility upgraded. Indicator: A 270-meter seawall constructed along the western and northern shorelines of the landfill site Progress/Status: The seawall will no longer push through. Instead, a fence is to be constructed along the western and northern shorelines of the landfill site. The fence is a part of the landfill site design in package W2. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: n Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: n Target year: 2027 Target value: y

Output: A high-temperature incinerator constructed, and waste disposal site and recycling facility upgraded. Indicator: A 9-13 tons/day high-temperature incinerator, with the capacity to incinerate menstrual and medical waste safely, constructed and operated using a DBM contract with a 5-year management contract Progress/Status: An environmental impact assessment (EIA) for the incinerator component is necessary before the start of the bidding process, as well as the terms of reference (TOR) for the scope of the EIA. The first version of the EIA TOR has been drafted is currently under review.
Q2 2025 update: During the project's MTR in December 2024 and subsequent communications in March 2025, it has been decided that the incinerator package will be removed from the project. A change in scope will be processed for this change.
Q3 2025 update: A change in scope is currently under process to confirm the removal of the incinerator from the project's scope. Target to be approved in Q4 2025.
Q4 2025: A mission was fielded in Nov 2025. Following this, the minor change will be finalized. Target approval moved to Q1 2026. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: 9

Output: A high-temperature incinerator constructed, and waste disposal site and recycling facility upgraded. Indicator: The dump site converted into a managed landfill with a new recycling facility Progress/Status: Preliminary works (cleaning and shifting of wastes) have been completed. The bidding document for solid waste management infrastructure has been prepared. Bidding is expected to commence within Q4 2025.
Q4 2025 update: SWM civil works have not been advertised yet. Target moved to Q1 2026. Required EPA review is ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: y

Output: Institutional capacity to sustain SWM service delivery and local engagement strengthened Indicator: A gender-sensitive solid waste collection and disposal operation plan developed and implemented Progress/Status: Community engagement specialist, community engagement officer has been recruited. Activities ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: y

Output: Institutional capacity to sustain SWM service delivery and local engagement strengthened Indicator: An SWM tariff framework established and operational, and a lower tariff levied on poor households, including all households headed by women Progress/Status: To enhance the sustainability of KALGOV's SWM operations, the first version of the KALGOV Financial Management Plan was drafted under the project. Development of the tariff framework and fee collection plan is ongoing. Data Source: PIU quarterly reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: y

Output: Municipal solid waste collection, transport, and disposal operations improved Indicator: Ebeye Hospital receives COVID-19 enhanced and sustainable medical waste collection service Progress/Status: For medical waste generated at the Ebeye Hospital, the hospital has an ongoing contract with a local private company for medical waste management. The company collects medical waste from the hospital and incinerate collected waste with a small incinerator located on the causeway in the north of Ebeye. The project will help the Ebeye Hospital and its contractor strengthen the existing medical waste management system (waste classification, segregation, storage, transport, and disposal) to make it safer and more sustainable.
